editorial:
Imagine sitting down to listen to a man who has completely made up his mind to leave this world. You get to know him not through action, but through his words as he explains why he feels he can no longer live in today's society. He talks about his lifelong fight for freedom and how he felt trapped by the times he lived in. It is a very personal experience where you feel like you are in a deep conversation with someone who is tired of the world but still finds things to laugh at. The vibe is quiet and reflective, focusing on his memories of the few women he loved, his close friends, and his father.

What really hits home is how the main actor handles the role. He manages to be sad but also funny and sarcastic, which keeps the movie from feeling too heavy. The pacing is slow, so you need to be in the right mood for a character study rather than a plot-driven story. If you enjoy movies that make you think about life and liberty, you should definitely give this a try.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the man completes his plan to end his own life. He views this act not as a defeat, but as the only way to finally be truly free from a world that never understood him. He stays sarcastic and calm until the very end. The movie wraps up by showing that he finally achieved the absolute freedom he spent his whole life chasing, leaving the viewer to think about his choices.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and deep conversations about life.
